issues.legal_issue: An aggrieved person may invoke a revisional jurisdiction that is expressed as exercisable by the government on its own motion.
material_facts: The landowners invoked the government's revisional jurisdiction to challenge an order made under the land-ceiling law.
The Corporation argued that only the government could initiate revision on its own motion.
issues.conclusion: The revisional proceeding could be initiated by an aggrieved party; the provision's reference to action on the government's own motion did not exclude that possibility.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Urban Land (Ceiling & Regulation) Act, 1976 empowers the State Government to call for and examine records on its own motion, but does not prevent an aggrieved party from inviting the government's attention to an order's alleged illegality or impropriety.

predicates.statutory_revision_proceeding: The proceeding asks a public authority to exercise a statutory power to review an order or proceeding.
predicates.party_is_aggrieved_by_order: A party claims that an order made under the governing law adversely affects that party.

issues.definition: When a statutory review proceeding is brought by a party adversely affected by the challenged order, that party may invoke the review jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory revision remedy conditioned on no appeal having been preferred is an alternative to appeal, not an additional remedy after appeal.
material_facts: The landowners had earlier filed an appeal concerning a later order in the land-ceiling proceedings.
They subsequently invoked the government's revisional jurisdiction in relation to the underlying proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The statutory revision remedy was alternative to an appeal and was not an additional or supplementary remedy over and above appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Urban Land (Ceiling & Regulation) Act, 1976 authorizes revision in cases against which no appeal has been preferred under the specified appeal provisions; the Court construed revision as an alternative, not supplementary, remedy.

predicates.statutory_revision_proceeding: The proceeding asks a public authority to exercise a statutory power to review an order or proceeding.
predicates.appeal_remedy_is_provided: The governing legal scheme provides an appeal remedy for the relevant kind of order or proceeding.
predicates.no_appeal_has_been_preferred: No appeal has been brought against the order or proceeding for which revision is sought.

issues.definition: Where a statutory review proceeding is available under a scheme that also provides appeal, and no appeal has been brought, review operates as an alternative to appeal rather than an additional remedy.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional power for which no limitation period is prescribed must be exercised within a reasonable time assessed in light of the circumstances.
material_facts: The governing law prescribed no period for invoking revision.

The landowners sought revision many years after the original order and after intervening appeals, a prior revision, vesting of the land, its assignment to the Corporation, payment, transfer of possession, and development activity.
The revisional authority set aside the original order without considering the delay, intervening circumstances, or subsequent events.
issues.conclusion: The revisional authority had to assess whether the power was invoked within a reasonable time, considering the delay and the circumstances; its failure to do so made its order legally infirm.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Urban Land (Ceiling & Regulation) Act, 1976 sets no limitation period, but the Court applied the reasonable-time principle in State of Gujarat v. Patel Raghav Natha, (1969) 2 SCC 187, and referred to Shailesh Jadavji Varia v. Sub-Registrar, Vadodara, (1996) 3 Guj LR 783 (FB). What is reasonable depends on the facts and nature of the order; there is no universal period.

predicates.statutory_revision_proceeding: The proceeding asks a public authority to exercise a statutory power to review an order or proceeding.
predicates.no_time_limit_fixed: The governing law does not prescribe a time limit for invoking the review power.
predicates.delay_or_intervening_events_exist: A substantial delay or material events between the challenged order and the review proceeding may affect whether review should be exercised.

issues.definition: When statutory review has no prescribed time limit and delay or intervening events exist, the review power must be exercised within a time reasonable in the circumstances.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose assigned interest in land may be affected by a revisional decision must receive a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
material_facts: The State had assigned land to the Corporation after the land vested in the State.
The Corporation paid the occupancy price, received possession, and was undertaking construction activity.
The revisional authority set aside the order concerning the land without making the Corporation a party or giving it notice and an opportunity to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The Corporation was an affected party and was entitled to notice and a hearing before the revisional authority decided the matter.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 34 of the Urban Land (Ceiling & Regulation) Act, 1976 requires a reasonable opportunity of being heard for a person affected by a revisional order. The Court applied the principles of natural justice and held that a party with an assigned interest and possession could not be treated as a mere beneficiary without an affected interest.

rule.if: administrative_revision_proceeding and third_party_has_assigned_interest and revision_decision_affects_interest and third_party_not_heard

predicates.administrative_revision_proceeding: A public authority is considering whether to revise an administrative order or proceeding.
predicates.third_party_has_assigned_interest: A person other than the original disputants has received an interest in the subject matter from a public authority.
predicates.revision_decision_affects_interest: The proposed revisional decision may impair or undo that person's interest in the subject matter.
predicates.third_party_not_heard: The person whose interest may be affected was not given notice and a reasonable opportunity to present a case before the decision.

issues.definition: In an administrative revision, when a third party has received an interest that the decision may impair, that party must be heard before the decision is made.

issues.legal_issue: An administrative order alleged to be invalid cannot simply be disregarded as void before it is set aside through appropriate proceedings.
material_facts: The original order determining excess land had not been challenged by the landowners in the earlier appeal.
The order stated that notice had been properly sent to the address supplied and treated the owners as served.

The landowners did not raise non-service or lack of hearing in their earlier appeal or revision, and the later revisional authority set the order aside without considering the earlier proceedings and subsequent events.
issues.conclusion: The original order could not be treated as void or illegal merely on the basis of an allegation of defective notice while it remained unchallenged; it remained effective unless set aside through appropriate proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the principle discussed in Smith v. East Elloe Rural District Council, 1956 AC 736, and State of Punjab v. Gurdev Singh, (1991) 4 SCC 1: an allegedly invalid order remains effective for its ostensible purpose unless appropriate legal proceedings establish its invalidity and set it aside. A party seeking a declaration of invalidity must use the proper remedy and comply with applicable procedural requirements.

predicates.challenge_to_administrative_order: A proceeding seeks to challenge an order made by an administrative authority.
predicates.invalidity_is_alleged: A party claims that the order is invalid or unlawful.
predicates.order_has_not_been_set_aside: No competent authority or court has set the challenged order aside through appropriate proceedings.

issues.definition: When an administrative order is challenged as invalid but has not been set aside, it remains effective until it is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of earlier proceedings solely for maintainability does not create a res judicata bar, although the history and delay in those proceedings remain relevant to a later revision.
material_facts: An earlier appeal was dismissed as not maintainable because it challenged an order for which appeal was unavailable.
A first revision was also dismissed as not maintainable.

The landowners later brought a second revision, and the Court held that the earlier dismissals did not bar it by res judicata but that the revisional authority still had to consider delay, reasons for not acting earlier, and intervening circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The earlier dismissals on maintainability grounds did not operate as res judicata, but the revisional authority was still required to consider the delay and circumstances before deciding whether to exercise revision.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted that res judicata did not apply to the earlier proceedings dismissed on maintainability grounds. That did not remove the duty under Section 34 of the Urban Land (Ceiling & Regulation) Act, 1976, read with the reasonable-time principle in State of Gujarat v. Patel Raghav Natha, (1969) 2 SCC 187, to consider delay, reasons for not approaching the authority earlier, and intervening circumstances.

predicates.later_statutory_revision_proceeding: A party brings a statutory proceeding to seek review after earlier proceedings concerning the dispute.
predicates.earlier_proceedings_dismissed_only_for_m: The earlier proceedings were dismissed because they could not be brought in that form, rather than after a decision on their merits.

issues.definition: When a later statutory review follows earlier proceedings dismissed only for maintainability, those dismissals do not bar review by res judicata.
